claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films possess significant deposition-induced residual stress.
Residual stresses create local variations in elastic energy within the films.
Local elastic-energy variations influence nucleation and growth of the magnetostructural phase.
The as-deposited films exhibit a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited films exhibit a large magnetocaloric entropy change with considerable thermal and magnetic hysteresis.
A controlled low-temperature post-deposition anneal can relieve residual stress in the films.
The proposed intervention is annealing at approximately 300–400 °C for a short duration in an inert atmosphere.
Stress relief will reduce residual strain and elastic-energy heterogeneity.
Reduced elastic-energy heterogeneity will produce a more uniform nucleation barrier for the transition.
A more homogeneous transformation-energy landscape will yield a broader and less hysteretic transition.
Annealed films will exhibit narrower thermal and magnetic hysteresis loops than the as-deposited control.
Annealing may cause a slight shift in the magnetostructural transition temperature.
The annealed films will retain peak magnetic entropy change within approximately 20% of the as-deposited value.
The predicted behavior applies during sub-1 T cycling near room temperature, approximately within ±20 K of the transition.
The predictions require annealing conditions that avoid grain growth, phase decomposition, or alteration of phase constitution.
The proposed annealing treatment will preserve the film's high surface-to-volume ratio.
Residual stress, phase structure, hysteresis, latent heat, magnetic entropy response, and adiabatic temperature change can be compared between identically deposited annealed and unannealed film sets.
Failure to reduce both measured residual stress and hysteresis significantly, or loss of more than approximately 20% of peak magnetic entropy change, is specified as rejection of the hypothesis.
